answer: Hardware-rooted remote attestation curbs Sybil attacks in agent networks processing dawn lidar scans of a basalt island. Each agent's Trusted Execution Environment signs a chip-unique ID, session key, and code hash over an epoch nonce, which verifiers check against vendor roots and deduplicate. Because fused silicon secrets resist VM cloning, attackers incur dedicated chip hardware per identity, though side-channel extraction or rented cloud enclaves can still break uniqueness.
